ai.description: Nagaland's Toad is a medium-sized bufonid with a mottled brown and yellowish-grey dorsum. It is distinguished by its prominent, elongated parotoid glands and heavily tuberculated skin.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Duttaphrynus nagalandensis* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, continuous cranial crest that extends from the snout to the parotoid glands.
ai.habitat: Duttaphrynus nagalandensis inhabits high-altitude subtropical evergreen forests in Nagaland, typically found near streams at elevations between 1,000 and 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: Nagaland's Toad is primarily nocturnal, emerging after dusk to forage for small invertebrates among the leaf litter of its moist, mountainous habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Duttaphrynus nagalandensis* is an oviparous breeder that lays eggs in strings within shallow pools. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically from May to July.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Duttaphrynus nagalandensis* is endemic to the high-altitude regions of Nagaland, India, specifically inhabiting mountainous areas at elevations above 1,500 meters.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Duttaphrynus nagalandensis* is a high-pitched, rhythmic series of pulsed notes typically heard near small, stagnant forest pools.
